items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: Betty Hall Jones, who is a very dear friend of mine

ctx.x: were talking about it at all the schools, you see. This was the way they had to do to make the money, because there was no such thing as telethons, today, where you can make hundreds of thousands of dollars at one pitch, you know. And he said, "Why don't you?" I says, "Well, I'm not known. These people that are going to appear on the show, like Betty Hutton and Bob Hope and many others," I said, "Well, they're all people who are very well known, they're famous people," I said, "Momma's not famous." And he said,…

So my aunt, Augusta Glover, called me and she said, "Listen," she says, "I've been reading about this show that they're going to have at the Hollywood High School, the March of Dimes thing." She says, "Why aren't you -- why don't you get onto that." Well, I think my friend Betty Hall Jones, who is a very dear friend of mine, and a very marvelous, magnificent entertainer, pianist and entertainer, and Betty and I had been friends for years. When I first came here I also met her. So she says, "Why don't you get on…

push her, you know. She was at that time boogie-woogie. Well, Betty comes from Kansas, and of course she had a great flair for boggie, you know, boogie-woogie. And of course she had gotten sort of into entertaining by this time. She had gotten away from, somewhat away from some of the boogie, but she was still, you know, using this thing.
